title: Web security basics
summary: The attacks every web app must defend against — injection, XSS, CSRF — plus transport, secrets and rate limiting, with the Java patterns that stop each one.
note:
1. Never trust input: validate, and use parameterised queries (no string SQL)
2. XSS: escape output; CSRF: tokens + SameSite cookies
3. Hash passwords (bcrypt), serve over HTTPS, keep secrets out of code
4. Rate-limit auth and expensive endpoints to blunt abuse
✎ In my words: ______________________________________________

recall.q: How do you stop SQL injection?
recall.a: Use parameterised queries / prepared statements so input is bound as data, never concatenated into the SQL string.

recall.q: XSS vs CSRF in one line each?
recall.a: XSS injects script into pages you serve (fix: escape output); CSRF tricks a logged-in browser into sending a request (fix: anti-CSRF token + SameSite).
As a salted, slow hash (bcrypt/argon2) — never plaintext or a fast hash like MD5/SHA-1.

shot.title: Top defences
shot.body:
| threat | fix |
|---|---|
| SQL injection | parameterised queries |
| XSS | escape/encode output |
| CSRF | token + SameSite cookie |
| sniffing | HTTPS everywhere |
| weak passwords | bcrypt/argon2 hash |
| abuse/brute force | rate limiting |

sections.title: Never trust input
sections.body: ✍️ Treat every client value as hostile. Validate type/length/range, and — critically — build SQL with **parameterised queries** so input is bound as data, never concatenated into the statement. JPA and `PreparedStatement` do this for you; hand-built SQL strings are where injection lives.

sections.title: XSS & CSRF
sections.body:
✍️ **XSS** (cross-site scripting): an attacker gets script into a page you serve, running in other users' browsers. Fix by **escaping output** and setting a Content-Security-Policy. **CSRF** (cross-site request forgery): a malicious page makes a logged-in user's browser send a request using its cookies. Fix with an anti-CSRF token and `SameSite` cookies.
- Mark auth cookies `HttpOnly` + `Secure` so script cannot read them.

sections.title: Transport, secrets & rate limiting
sections.body: ✍️ Serve everything over **HTTPS** so tokens and data are not sniffed. Hash passwords with **bcrypt/argon2** (slow + salted), never a fast hash. Keep secrets in env/vault config, not in source or git. **Rate-limit** login and expensive endpoints to blunt brute-force and abuse — the same throttle pattern used at the API gateway.
